task.task_title: record what the merge actually did
task.display_name: record what the merge actually did
task.spec:
Target: config/scripts/orchestration-merge-gate.mjs (the merge command).
Change: after a run is merged, the schedule ledger still holds only dispatches and verdicts — nothing says which branch landed, onto which base, in which order, with which commits. That is exactly the record a post-mortem needs, so `merge --execute` must append one append-only entry per merged branch carrying branch, base, resulting commit and merge order, and the gate must expose those entries through the same view command that reads the ledger.
Constraints: the existing verify / merge / record-done behaviour must not change; a merge that aborts on conflict must not append an entry claiming success (append an explicit aborted entry instead, naming the conflicting branch); append-only — never rewrite an existing line; the flag must be explicit, so a plain `merge --execute` without it keeps today's behaviour.
Write set: config/scripts/orchestration-merge-gate.mjs, config/scripts/orchestration-schedule-ledger.mjs (only if the view cannot already read an unknown event type).
Acceptance: on a real temporary git repository, a `merge --execute --record-to <ledger>` appends one readable entry per merged branch, and the conflict path appends an aborted entry instead of a success; `node --test config/scripts/orchestration-merge-gate.test.mjs` stays green.
